claim.summary: If every finite competitor has real-part gap at least δ, every residual is bounded by B, c is nonnegative, and B < 2*c*δ, then every listed competitor has strictly smaller shifted squared modulus after the shift.
claim.positive_gap_condition: forall p in competitors, δ <= a - p.1
claim.conclusion: forall p in competitors, shiftedSqMod c p.1 p.2 < shiftedSqMod c a b

proves: single computable scalar inequality B < 2*c*δ implies dominance under gap and residual assumptions
does_not_prove: actual spectrum extraction from a matrix
construction of B from a matrix spectrum
construction of δ from a matrix spectral gap
strict spectral-abscissa hypothesis for a matrix eigenvalue
that a strict-abscissa eigenvalue of a real matrix is real
